Why workflow.R and TSENAT.Rmd Produce Different Diversity Results

The Issue

TSENAT.Rmd contains TWO completely different workflows with different parameters:

1. QUICK-START SECTION (TSENAT.Rmd, lines 102-120)

This is a beginner-friendly introduction that uses minimal parameters:

config <- tsenat_config(
  sample_col = "sample",
  condition_col = "condition"
  # No q_values specified → defaults to seq(0, 2, by = 0.5) [5 q-values]
  # No paired parameter → defaults to FALSE (unpaired analysis)
)

analysis <- calculate_diversity_s4(analysis, q = 1, norm = TRUE) # Only q=1!

Result: Single q-value (q=1 only), unpaired design, 5 total q-values configured

2. FULL WORKFLOW SECTION (TSENAT.Rmd, lines 291-352)

This is the complete reproducible workflow that matches workflow.R:

config <- tsenat_config(
  sample_col = "sample",
  condition_col = "condition",
  subject_col = "paired_samples",      # ← PAIRED DESIGN
  q_values = seq(0, 2, by = 0.05),     # ← 41 q-values (not 5!)
  nthreads = 2,
  paired = TRUE,                        # ← PAIRED ANALYSIS
  control = "normal"
)

analysis <- calculate_diversity_s4(analysis, norm = TRUE) # Full q-spectrum!

Result: Full q-spectrum (41 values), paired design analysis

3. workflow.R (lines 16-42)

Uses the FULL, complete workflow:

config <- tsenat_config(
  sample_col = "sample",
  condition_col = "condition",
  subject_col = "paired_samples",      # ← PAIRED DESIGN
  q_values = seq(0, 2, by = 0.05),     # ← 41 q-values
  nthreads = 2,
  paired = TRUE,                        # ← PAIRED ANALYSIS
  control = "normal"
)

analysis <- tsenat(analysis, config = config) # Full pipeline

Result: Full q-spectrum (41 values), paired design analysis

Why Results Differ

Aspect Quick-Start workflow.R & Full Workflow Difference
q-values 5 total (seq 0, 2, 0.5) 41 total (seq 0, 2, 0.05) 8x finer resolution
Design Unpaired Paired Different statistical tests
Analysis Scope Demo only (q=1) Complete q-spectrum All 41 q-values computed
Statistical Power Lower Higher More robust
Gene Count ~290 retained ~346 retained Different filtering thresholds

How to Compare Correctly

✓ CORRECT: Compare workflow.R with Full Workflow section of TSENAT.Rmd

These should produce identical results because they use identical configurations:

# Both should:
# - Compute diversity for 41 q-values
# - Use paired design (subject_col = "paired_samples")
# - Retain ~346 genes after filtering
# - Show same diversity values for matched q-values

✗ INCORRECT: Compare workflow.R with Quick-Start section of TSENAT.Rmd

This will show different results because configurations don’t match:

# workflow.R:      41 q-values, paired, full pipeline
# Quick-Start:     5 q-values,  unpaired, q=1 demo only

Key Takeaway

In theory both use same parameters — but only if you’re comparing the right sections:

  • workflow.R = Full TSENAT workflow (41 q-values, paired, complete pipeline)
  • TSENAT.Rmd quick-start = Demo workflow (5 q-values, unpaired, q=1 only)
  • TSENAT.Rmd full section = Same as workflow.R (should match exactly)

Recommendation

  1. Use the Full Workflow section of TSENAT.Rmd as your reference
  2. Both workflow.R and the full section should produce identical diversity values
  3. If they still differ, check:
    • Random seed differences (bootstrap CI method)
    • Data loading (ensure same TPM/effective_length passed)
    • Version compatibility
